A1.justification: v1.pdf and v2.pdf describe the same work, with matching authors, title, algorithms, and main contributions. Their text, equations, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of the removed calculation-code appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and numerical evaluations of analytical constants in Appendix E, not experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Section 5 explicitly leaves empirical benchmarking to future work.

after.justification: v2 retains theoretical results and numerical theorem instantiations in Appendix E. It adds no empirical study and continues to defer empirical benchmarking in Section 5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain sample splitting, robust spectral initialization on label-weighted covariates, robust gradient descent, and normalization. Algorithm 3 clarifies its parameter names and writes the equivalent step size using alpha and gamma; the procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates training or test datasets. The same six analytical examples remain: Logistic, Tanh, Probit, phase retrieval, GeLU, and Swish. No evaluated task or population is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Table 1 retains the same literature entries and compares theoretical guarantees; its revised descriptions do not constitute changes to an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to Gaussian-moment calculations and certified radii concern theoretical bounds, rather than data splits, evaluation metrics, or experimental budgets.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or error analyses. The revised robustness arguments are mathematical proofs, and Appendix E continues to instantiate theoretical constants.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probabilistic guarantees are theoretical and do not represent experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 updates numerical constants for the retained six links. For example, Logistic's radius changes from 0.371 to 0.060, and phase retrieval's radius changes from 0.00164 to 0.031, with phi1 changing from 608 to 682. ESC, mu, and mu1 remain unchanged. These are revised theorem instantiations under a changed curvature bound, not comparable-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.1 replaces the third-derivative-based complexity measure with fourth-moment envelopes of f' and f'', explicitly requires positive curvature, and changes the radius condition to 6 sqrt(15) R C_lip(R) <= mu. Section 3 and Appendix B replace the mean-value argument with an integral proof and add Gaussian mixed-moment Lemma B.2. Appendix D also revises the gradient-covariance proof, correctly uses conditional noise moments, and fixes the normalization inequality. Appendix E updates the corresponding derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same headline claims: dimension-independent convex basins, efficient robust initialization, and near-linear recovery with O(sigma sqrt(epsilon)) error for a broad class of non-monotonic SIMs. The revision changes their mathematical support and formal assumptions.

C2.justification: Remark 2.1 removes the assertion that violating the regularity condition necessarily implies an unbounded response second moment under Gaussian covariates. Appendix E also explains when direct Gaussian-moment calculations yield sharper radii than global derivative bounds. The principal limitations and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix E.4 supplies a complete numerical calculation script, including JAX precision settings, SciPy quadrature, integration limits, optimization, and root-finding choices. v2 removes this entire implementation without replacement code or access instructions. Its clearer mathematical calculation instructions do not preserve those implementation details.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a non-degeneracy qualification for Plan et al. (2017), explaining failure for even links with symmetric noise; Table 1 changes that entry from SIM to Odd SIM. Huang et al. (2026)'s sample complexity changes from tilde-O(d) to O(d), matching the retained prose. The cited-work set is unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision locally rewrites proof explanations and numerical derivations, moves the population-loss definition into the preliminaries, clarifies notation, removes an unfinished sentence in Remark 4.1, and adds an acknowledgement of the earlier proof error. Appendix E.4 disappears, but the main narrative and section organization remain.

P2.justification: v2 increases vertical spacing and reflows text, equations, and algorithm boxes. Both tables retain their basic organization, with a shorter Table 2 caption and modest formatting changes. No plotted figures or new table structures are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs a foundational deficiency in Theorem 3.1: the problematic mean-value expansion and Gaussian treatment of an interpolation point are replaced by an exact integral argument with controlled moments. Related covariance and normalization proof corrections further strengthen mathematical reliability. Removing the calculation script reduces reproducibility, but the repair of the central convex-basin argument provides a substantial net improvement.
